t: A trolley is moving. Four forces are acting on it. Can you put them in the right place?
Four forces push and pull a moving trolley. Can you place each one correctly?
A moving trolley has four forces on it: push, friction, gravity, and the normal force. Assign each to its direction.
Identify the four forces on a body in motion and their directions. This is a free-body diagram.
sub: Every force has a direction. Get all four right to finish the module.
Push goes one way, friction another. Gravity and the normal force are vertical. Place them all.
A free-body diagram shows every force and its direction. Build one correctly to finish.
The free-body diagram is the foundational tool of mechanics. Constructing it correctly is the prerequisite for every force analysis.

question: A trolley sits on the ground, not moving. Which way does the ground push it?
A trolley is at rest on the ground. Which direction does the ground push it?
A stationary trolley on a surface: what is the direction of the normal force?
What is the direction of the normal force on a body at rest on a horizontal surface?
options: Up — the ground pushes up against gravity
Down — the ground pushes it into the ground
Sideways — the ground does not push vertically
stages.outcome: Up — the ground pushes up against gravity
note: The ground is doing something. Guess which way.
Predict. The ground is pushing — but which way?
The normal force has a direction. Predict it.
The normal force is perpendicular to the surface. Predict its direction.

t: Put each force in the right direction. Push goes forward, friction goes backward, gravity goes down, and the normal force goes up.
Place each force arrow in its correct direction. Push: forward. Friction: backward. Gravity: down. Normal force: up.

name: All forces correct
Complete free-body diagram
pass: Every force is in its right place. That is a correct force diagram.
The free-body diagram is complete and correct. All four forces are assigned to their proper directions.
fail: Some forces are in the wrong direction. Check which arrow points where.
One or more forces are misassigned. Verify: push forward, friction back, gravity down, normal up.

name: Horizontal forces
Horizontal pair
pass: Push and friction are correctly placed — the horizontal forces are right.
Horizontal pair correct: push forward, friction backward.
fail: The horizontal forces are wrong. Push goes forward, friction goes backward.
Horizontal pair incorrect. Push is forward; friction opposes motion (backward).

name: Vertical forces
Vertical pair
pass: Gravity and the normal force are correct — the vertical forces balance.
Vertical pair correct: gravity down, normal force up.
fail: The vertical forces are wrong. Gravity pulls down, the normal force pushes up.
Vertical pair incorrect. Gravity acts downward; the normal force is perpendicular to the surface (upward on a horizontal surface).

win: You built a correct force diagram. Every force has a direction, and every direction has its force.
The free-body diagram is complete and correct. You can now analyse any force problem — this is the starting point of all mechanics.
lose: Some forces are misplaced. Push forward, friction back, gravity down, normal up. Try again.
The diagram is incomplete or incorrect. Review: push is forward, friction opposes motion, gravity is downward, normal force is perpendicular to the surface. Adjust and re-test.

t: That diagram you just built is called a force diagram. It is how physicists see moving things.
A diagram showing every force on a thing is called a force diagram. It is the first step in solving any force problem.
A force diagram (or free-body diagram) shows every force acting on an object and its direction. It is the starting point of every mechanics problem.
A free-body diagram (FBD) isolates a body and represents all external forces as vectors. It is the prerequisite for applying ΣF = ma.
sub: Every force problem starts with one of these. Get the forces right, and the rest is arithmetic.
Physicists and engineers draw these before every calculation. The diagram is the problem; the numbers come after.
The FBD is universal: the same tool solves trolley problems, bridge design, orbital mechanics, and crash analysis.
The FBD externalises the force analysis. Errors in FBDs propagate into every subsequent calculation — correctness here is non-negotiable.

t: Engineers draw force diagrams before building anything — bridges, cars, rockets. Wrong diagram, wrong building.
Every bridge, car, and rocket starts with a force diagram. Get the forces wrong and the structure fails.
Structural engineering is force diagrams at scale. Every beam, cable, and bolt is analysed with a free-body diagram before it is built.
Finite element analysis is the computational descendant of the FBD. Every engineering simulation begins with the same question: what forces act on this body, and in what direction?

q: What does a force diagram show?
What is the purpose of a free-body diagram in mechanics?
options: A picture showing every force on a thing and which way it points
A picture of the thing itself, with no forces
A list of numbers about how heavy things are
why: A force diagram shows the thing and every force on it, each pointing the right way. It is how you see what is pushing what.
A force diagram (free-body diagram) shows an object and every force acting on it, with arrows for direction. It is the starting point for any force calculation.
A free-body diagram isolates a body and draws every external force as a vector. It is the visual representation of ΣF = ma.
An FBD externalises the force model: the body is isolated, and every external force is drawn as a vector. It is the prerequisite for applying Newton's second law correctly.
